proposed.title: Warehouse source auth options: the unpicked option's nested config must not block the save, and auth_type can arrive in two shapes
answers: BigQuery source setup fails with Required field 'private_key' is missing
new source wizard error lists JSON key fields I never typed
service account selected but validation complains about key file
auth_type is a string instead of a dict in job_inputs
proposed.body:
Symptom: a BigQuery source using a Google Cloud service account is rejected at the end of the wizard with "Required field '<key file field>' is missing" errors. Also, a key file that isn't a service account key shows the same raw field list.
Root cause: the wizard sends the credential fields of both auth options. The shared walker common/config.py:validate_config checks the nested BigQueryAuthTypeConfigKeyFileConfig and reports every field as missing, even when that option wasn't picked.
Fix pattern: in bigquery/source.py:BigQuerySource.validate_config, drop the errors built with missing_field_error(...) for every key-file dataclass field and recompute is_valid. Then check only the selected option yourself. key_file needs every field present and non-empty, because the shared check only tests presence. service_account needs google_cloud_service_account_integration_id. Return product-language messages, never internal field names.
Invariant: auth_type can be a dict ({selection, key_file, ...}) or a bare string naming the option, with the credential fields at the top level of job_inputs. Handle both shapes. If you return early on the string shape, sources save with no credential.
Constraints: the per-option credential fields are optional on the form, so this source-level check is the only thing stopping a credential-less source. The fix stays in the source on purpose. Changing the shared walker to skip unpicked options would affect every source.
proposed.applies: Warehouse sources with a select-container auth field (BigQuery and similar) in products/warehouse_sources/backend/temporal/data_imports/sources/

proposed.title: Use missing_field_error to match or replace generic required-field errors from source config validation
answers: how to replace Required field ... is missing with a custom message for a source
where is the Required field error string built
filter required-field errors in a source validate_config
proposed.body:
common/config.py:missing_field_error(field_name) is the one place that builds the "Required field '<name>' is missing" string, and validate_config uses it.
A source that wants to suppress or reword those errors should build its match set from missing_field_error. BigQuery does this: _KEY_FILE_FIELD_ERRORS is built from dataclasses.fields(BigQueryAuthTypeConfigKeyFileConfig). Don't copy the literal string into the source.
Build the field list from the generated config dataclass (generated_configs/<source>), not a hand-written list, so it stays in sync when the generated config changes.
Tests check that no returned error contains "Required field". API tests in backend/tests/api/test_external_data_source.py check the user-facing message text, so update them when you change the copy.
proposed.applies: Any warehouse source overriding validate_config on top of the shared config walker

proposed.title: Codex turns had no trace id: ratings on Codex Slack answers opened nothing
answers: Slack rating on a codex run points at no trace
codex generations each appear in their own trace of one in AI observability
why is $ai_trace_id different for every codex request
turn-complete traceId missing for codex adapter
proposed.body:
Symptom: A rating on a PostHog Slack answer from a Codex run resolves to nothing. In AI observability, each of the run's generations sits alone in a trace of one. Claude runs group correctly.
Root cause: Codex sends no trace header, so the gateway stamps a fresh `$ai_trace_id` per request. Claude's CLI mints a per-turn `traceparent`, which the gateway reads (ai-gateway#496). The Codex adapter also mints its own turn-complete notification without `traceId`, and `AgentServer.turnTraceId` (formerly `promptResultTraceId`) only read `PromptResponse._meta.traceId`.
Fix pattern: In products/desktop/packages/agent/src/server/agent-server.ts:configureEnvironment, set `openaiCustomHeaders["X-PostHog-Trace-Id"] = taskRunId` for codex only. Then record that header value as `stampedRunTraceId` and use it as the fallback trace id: in `AgentServer.turnTraceId` for command results and relays, and through acp-extensions.ts:withTurnTraceId for wire turn-complete notifications.
Constraints: The run is the finest granularity available because Codex takes gateway headers only at process spawn (`model_providers.posthog.http_headers`), so there is no per-turn hook like Claude's `traceparent-hook`. An adapter-reported traceId always wins over the fallback.
proposed.applies: products/desktop/packages/agent server: gateway trace ids for codex runs and turn-complete/rating plumbing

proposed.title: X-PostHog-Trace-Id is codex-only, and the fallback trace id must come from the stamped header
answers: can I set X-PostHog-Trace-Id for claude runs
where should the turn trace id for a rating be resolved
why not infer trace id from runtime_adapter in forward_pending_message
stampedRunTraceId semantics
proposed.body:
Invariant 1: Never send `X-PostHog-Trace-Id` on Claude gateway headers. The gateway ranks this header above `traceparent`, so Claude's per-turn trace ids would collapse into one id for the whole run. Enforced in agent-server.ts:configureEnvironment (`taskRunId && runtimeAdapter === "codex"`) and tested in agent-server.configure-environment.test.ts ("names the run as X-PostHog-Trace-Id for codex only").
Invariant 2: `AgentServer.stampedRunTraceId` is read straight from `gatewayEnv.openaiCustomHeaders["X-PostHog-Trace-Id"]`. It is never inferred from `runtime_adapter`, and it is reset unconditionally on every init so a re-init does not keep a stale run's id. A Codex run with no `AI_GATEWAY_TOKEN` falls back to the Python gateway and gets no stamp. Inferring the id would point a rating at a trace with no generations.
Convention: Resolve the turn trace id in the agent-server, next to the stamp. Do not resolve it in the Temporal activity `forward_pending_message` under products/tasks/. That activity never sees the direct relay or the turn-complete event paths, and three reviewers rejected that approach.
proposed.applies: Any change to gateway headers or turn trace id resolution in products/desktop/packages/agent/src/server/agent-server.ts

proposed.title: Where a turn's trace id reaches ratings: three agent-server paths plus the wire tap
answers: which paths carry the turn trace id to slack ratings
where is turn-complete traceId added before the session log
how does agent-design stream get traceId for a turn
proposed.body:
A rating can arrive by three paths, and each needs the turn trace id:
- The command result the Slack relay reads, and the direct relay. Both go through `AgentServer.turnTraceId(result)` → `broadcastTurnComplete(stopReason, traceId)`, which appears at three prompt-handling call sites in agent-server.ts.
- The turn-complete ACP notification read by the agent-design stream. adapters/acp-connection.ts:installWireTaps applies `withTurnTraceId(message, config.stampedRunTraceId)` to it.
In installWireTaps, the stamp is applied before `logWriter.appendNotification`, because a thread reload reads the stored copy rather than the broadcast one. Any new enrichment of wire messages must also happen before the log write.
`withTurnTraceId` only touches `POSTHOG_NOTIFICATIONS.TURN_COMPLETE` messages that have object params and no string `traceId`. It returns the same object in every other case. `stampedRunTraceId` is passed to the connection through `AcpConnectionConfig.stampedRunTraceId`.
proposed.applies: products/desktop/packages/agent turn-complete / trace id propagation

proposed.title: Freshness checks must read ExternalDataSchema.last_run_at, never last_synced_at alone; don't advance last_synced_at on zero-row runs
answers: why is last_synced_at not updated when a sync imports nothing
how do I tell when a warehouse schema last ran
schema shows stale / stopped syncing but jobs run on schedule
should I advance last_synced_at on a zero-batch v3 run
proposed.body:
Invariant: `last_synced_at` is also the signals watermark (`partition_field > last_synced_at`). The v3 pipeline deliberately does not advance it on a run that extracts zero rows (`pipeline_v3/pipeline.py:PipelineV3._stamp_full_run` writes only `sync_type_config.last_full_run_at`). If it did advance, rows arriving late with a partition value between two quiet runs would never emit a signal. That is why #104604 rejected the change and this PR kept that decision.
Which stamp each kind of run moves: a run that loads rows moves both stamps. A v3 zero-row run moves only `last_full_run_at`. A fast return on a negative probe moves only `last_synced_at`.
So any check that asks "when did a sync last run" (stale warnings, stall detection) must use `products/warehouse_sources/backend/models/external_data_schema.py:ExternalDataSchema.last_run_at`, which is the max of both. If you read only `last_synced_at`, a schema whose source is simply quiet gets reported as stalled or stale.
Use `ExternalDataSchema.last_full_run` to parse `last_full_run_at`. It returns None for a string that does not parse or has no timezone, so a naive stamp never counts as fresh. `create_job_model.py:_fast_return_eligible` and `sync_status.py:_is_stale` both use these properties. Don't hand-roll the parsing again.
proposed.applies: Any data-warehouse code that judges sync freshness or writes sync timestamps on ExternalDataSchema

proposed.title: Quiet schemas reported as stalled and auto-repaired by the stalled-schedule sweep
answers: customer told their sync stopped but scheduled syncs run fine
REPAIRED_SCHEMA_ERROR written on a schema that never stalled
stalled schedule sweep false positive for sources with no new data
repair_stalled_schema rewrote a healthy schedule
proposed.body:
Symptom: a schema on a regular schedule (for example every 6h) whose source has no new rows was reported as stalled. Repair then rewrote its schedule and wrote `REPAIRED_SCHEMA_ERROR`, which tells the customer PostHog restarted a sync that had never stopped.
Root cause: `products/warehouse_sources/backend/stalled_schedules.py:stalled_schema_queryset` measured silence only from `last_synced_at`. That stamp does not move on v3 zero-row runs, so a quiet schema drifted past `missed_intervals x sync_frequency_interval`.
Fix pattern: annotate `latest_run_at = Greatest(last_synced_at, <guarded cast of sync_type_config.last_full_run_at>)` and use it for three things: the `stalled_after` window, the `order_by` in `find_stalled_schemas`, and `StalledSchema.stalled_for`. Postgres GREATEST skips NULLs, so a missing or unusable run stamp falls back to `last_synced_at`.
Constraints: a schema whose run stamp is also old must still be reported. `test_a_schema_whose_runs_also_stopped_is_still_stalled` checks this. Keep the order key and `stalled_for` on the same stamp as the predicate.
proposed.applies: stalled_schedules.py sweep and the repair_stalled_schema management command

proposed.title: Filter on JSON timestamps in SQL before LIMIT, and regex-guard the cast
answers: how to compare sync_type_config.last_full_run_at in a queryset
Postgres error casting JSON string to timestamp
why not filter stalled schemas in Python after the query
naive timestamp read in session timezone
proposed.body:
Convention seen in `products/warehouse_sources/backend/stalled_schedules.py:stalled_schema_queryset`: `sync_type_config.last_full_run_at` is free-form JSON. Before casting it, check it with `When(sync_type_config__last_full_run_at__regex=_AWARE_ISO_TIMESTAMP, then=Cast(KeyTextTransform(...), DateTimeField()))` and default to NULL. Without that guard, Postgres raises on a string it cannot parse and reads a naive stamp in the session zone, which invents freshness. The SQL guard mirrors the Python rule in `ExternalDataSchema.last_full_run`: accept only ISO stamps with an offset or Z.
Do the filtering in SQL so the sweep and repair command can keep their `LIMIT`. Filtering in Python after the LIMIT let excluded rows fill every slot. Filtering in Python before it loaded every candidate on each hourly sweep.
Tests: `test_an_unusable_run_stamp_falls_back_to_the_sync_stamp` (unparseable and naive cases) and `find_stalled_schemas(limit=1)` with the excluded row sorted first.
proposed.applies: Django querysets in warehouse_sources that compare timestamps stored inside the sync_type_config JSON

proposed.title: Liquid merge tags in workflow emails must never contain double quotes; use dot access or single-quoted brackets
answers: workflow email link href breaks after inserting a person property merge tag
Liquid error expected "|" before filter in email template
merge tag renders blank / empty value in sent email
how should person property merge tags be quoted
proposed.body:
Symptom: a person property inserted from the email editor's merge-tag menu breaks a link (`href` cut short, Liquid parse error `expected "|" before filter`) or silently sends an empty value.
Root cause: the menu built `{{person.properties["name"]}}` in frontend/src/scenes/hog-functions/email-templater/emailTemplaterLogic.tsx; a double quote ends a double-quoted HTML attribute, and when it reaches the renderer entity-encoded (`"`) the decoder in nodejs/src/cdp/utils/liquid.ts does not decode it, so the tag resolves to ''.
Fix pattern: generate tags through `buildPersonPropertyMergeValue`: dot access for names matching `/^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/`, otherwise `['...']` with backslashes and `'` escaped. This matches `buildDelayExpression` in products/workflows stepDelayLogic.
Constraints: applies to any code that emits Liquid/merge-tag strings that may end up in HTML attributes. The liquid.ts decoder gap (`"`, `%22`) is still open, so do not count on the renderer to decode double quotes. Tests in emailTemplaterLogic.test.ts cover `$`-prefixed, spaced, dotted and apostrophe names.
proposed.applies: Email templater merge tags and any other generated Liquid expressions for messaging/workflows

proposed.title: frontend/src must not import from products/* (duplicate small pure helpers instead)
answers: can I import a helper from products/workflows into frontend/src
reuse buildDelayExpression in the email templater
cross-product import rule in the frontend
proposed.body:
Frontend rules forbid importing across `products/*` into `frontend/src`. Importing a helper from a product logic file (e.g. `buildDelayExpression` in products/workflows stepDelayLogic) would also pull in a kea logic module connected to `workflowLogic`.
Pattern used: write a small pure helper next to the consumer (`buildPersonPropertyMergeValue` in frontend/src/scenes/hog-functions/email-templater/emailTemplaterLogic.tsx) and add a comment pointing to the sibling implementation, so the two stay in sync by hand.
If you change the quoting/escaping in one of them, check the other.
proposed.applies: Shared logic between frontend/src scenes and products/* frontends

proposed.title: Prompt reference listings must be capped at MAX_ACTIVE_REFERENCE_RESULTS and ordered in SQL before slicing
answers: label move/delete error message lists thousands of prompt names
why is the referencing prompts list truncated to 100
how to add a new prompt reference listing helper
huge error body when deleting a label on a widely used partial
proposed.body:
Symptom: moving or deleting a prompt label used by a partial that thousands of prompts reference returned an enormous error message listing every parent prompt name.
Root cause: products/ai_observability/backend/prompt_references.py:get_active_parents_referencing_label was the only reference listing with no result cap, and its names are joined into label-move/label-delete error messages and dialogs.
Fix pattern: every reference listing in prompt_references.py ends with `.order_by(<name field>)[:MAX_ACTIVE_REFERENCE_RESULTS]` (100 entries), the same as its sibling helpers such as get_active_references_to. Ordering happens in SQL before the slice, so the capped subset is deterministic (the first N by name) and not an arbitrary set of rows.
Constraints: callers may treat a non-empty result only as "is referenced". That stays correct past the cap. Do not use len() of these lists as the true reference count. If you need an exact count, write a separate count query. Covered by posthog/api/test/test_llm_prompt.py:TestLLMPromptDependenciesAPI.test_label_parent_listing_is_capped, which creates cap+1 parents.
proposed.applies: Any helper in products/ai_observability/backend/prompt_references.py that lists referencing prompts for error messages/UI

proposed.title: Replay Vision async activities must evict stale Django DB connections first (track_activity)
answers: observation never gets a thumbnail after a database blip
async replay vision activity fails on first attempt after connection drop
where are stale db connections closed for replay vision temporal activities
connection already closed in async ORM call in temporal activity

proposed.title: Read-only impersonation 403s on read-only POST endpoints; allowlist the exact action, never the prefix
answers: support staff impersonating get 403 impersonation_read_only on a POST endpoint
audience count / blast radius never loads while impersonating
how do I let a read-only impersonation session call a POST that only reads
why does the workflow builder fail during read-only impersonation
proposed.body:
Symptom: during a read-only impersonation session a feature that reads through a POST (filters in the body, e.g. workflow audience sizing `hog_flows/user_blast_radius`) never loads, and the request fails with `403 impersonation_read_only`.
Root cause: posthog/middleware.py:ImpersonationReadOnlyMiddleware rejects every non-idempotent method before the viewset runs, so the viewset's own permissions/scopes never get a say. It is fail-closed and only lets through entries in posthog/middleware.py:READ_ONLY_IMPERSONATION_ALLOWLISTED_PATHS.
Fix pattern: first confirm the action writes nothing (trace its helpers). Then add one `("POST", re.compile(r"^/api/(environments|projects)/([0-9]+|@current)/<prefix>/<action>/?$"))` entry with a comment saying why it only reads. Name the exact action(s), because prefixes like `hog_flows/` and `logs/` also host writing actions (publish, run, bulk_delete, CRUD). The `environments` alternative follows the other entries' style. EnvironmentsRewriteMiddleware rewrites the path to `/api/projects/...` anyway.
Constraints: never allowlist an endpoint that spends a token or dispatches work (e.g. hog_flows `run`, `batch_jobs`). Add the allowed path to posthog/test/test_middleware.py:TestImpersonationReadOnlyMiddleware.test_read_only_impersonation_allows_allowlisted_post. Add writing siblings under the same prefix to test_read_only_impersonation_blocks_mutating_siblings, so a later edit that widens the regex fails CI. Changing how the middleware decides "read-only" (e.g. having it ask the viewset) is a platform change that needs its own security-reviewed PR. As of this PR, `POST feature_flags/user_blast_radius` was still blocked; sibling PR #105805 handles it.
proposed.applies: Any POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE endpoint that must work during read-only impersonation (posthog/middleware.py allowlist)

proposed.title: Per-partition Prometheus gauges must drop revoked partitions' series, or alerts see stale values
answers: false IngestionAnalyticsSinglePartitionDelayed page for a partition that is not behind
latest_processed_timestamp_ms stale after kafka rebalance
pod keeps exporting metrics for partitions it no longer owns
how to clear gauge labels on partition revoke
proposed.body:
Symptom: on-call gets an IngestionAnalyticsSinglePartitionDelayed page for a partition that is not behind, often an idle partition, after a rebalance.
Root cause: nodejs/src/ingestion/ingestion-consumer.ts:latestOffsetTimestampGauge kept the series of partitions the pod gave up in a rebalance. That frozen value kept getting older, and the alert's `max by (groupId, topic, partition)` picked it up whenever the new owner had no series yet.
Fix pattern: pass a revoke hook as the second argument of kafkaConsumer.connect. In IngestionConsumer.onPartitionsRevoked, call `gauge.remove({ topic, partition, groupId: this.groupId })` for each revoked partition, using the full label set. After this, only the current owner exports a partition.
Constraints: this applies to any gauge labelled by partition that an alert aggregates with max or min. common_ingestion_latest_processed_timestamp_ms in the common ingestion consumer still has the same stale-series problem; it was left out of scope because the analytics alert does not read it. Trade-off: if a new owner stalls before it processes its first message, the partition has no series and this alert stays silent. The all-partitions and stopped-consuming alerts still catch a stalled lane.
Test: ingestion-consumer.serial.test.ts gets the hook with `jest.mocked(ingester['kafkaConsumer'].connect).mock.calls[0][1]`, then checks `latestOffsetTimestampGauge.get()` values filtered by groupId. Call `.reset()` on the gauge first, because the registry is global.
proposed.applies: nodejs ingestion consumers that export per-partition Prometheus metrics

proposed.title: onPartitionsRevoked hook on KafkaConsumerInterface.connect: v2 awaits it before unassigning, v1 fires it after unassigning
answers: how do I run code when kafka partitions are revoked
does the revoke hook run before or after unassign
onPartitionsRevoked consumer v1 vs v2 difference
react to rebalance in a nodejs kafka consumer
proposed.body:
KafkaConsumerInterface.connect (nodejs/src/common/kafka/consumer/index.ts) takes an optional second argument, `onPartitionsRevoked(revokedPartitions: Assignment[]) => Promise<void>`. Both consumer implementations must support it.
KafkaConsumerV2 awaits the hook before it unassigns the partitions. The analytics lanes run v2 (CONSUMER_USE_V2).
KafkaConsumer (v1, consumer-v1.ts) stores the hook in connect. Its revoke path calls the hook after unassign and resetRebalanceCoordination, fire-and-forget. Errors are only logged as `partition_revoked_handler_failed`.
When you write a hook: keep it fast, and don't count on it running before unassign. Under v1 it runs late and its failures never surface.
v1 only sees revokes because its `false` rebalance mode (where node-rdkafka rebalanced on its own) was removed in #105238. Don't bring that mode back, or the hook will never fire.
The v1 test in consumer-v1.test.ts sets `consumer['onPartitionsRevoked']` directly and checks that it is called with the revoked assignments.
proposed.applies: nodejs/src/common/kafka/consumer implementations and their callers

proposed.title: Default insight list order must use an indexed column (-last_modified_at, -pk), not the vestigial Insight.order
answers: Why is the insights API slow when no order param is passed?
Insight list endpoint takes tens of seconds per page / pins web workers
What is the default sort order of /api/projects/:id/insights/?
Is it safe to sort insights by the `order` field?
proposed.body:
Symptom: API clients listing insights without an `order` query param wait tens of seconds per page; every offset page repeats the cost, and the load hits the shared Postgres primary.
Root cause: products/product_analytics/backend/presentation/insight.py:InsightViewSet.order_queryset fell back to `order_by("order")`. `Insight.order` is a vestigial nullable integer with no index (NULL on almost every row), so Postgres scanned and sorted the whole project, and pagination was non-deterministic (all rows in one NULL group).
Fix pattern: default to `order_by("-last_modified_at", "-pk")`. The partial index `dashboarditem_team_lmod_idx` on `(team_id, -last_modified_at) WHERE NOT deleted` covers it, so the sort can seek and the LIMIT stops early. This also stops the correlated `with_last_viewed_at` subquery from running for every row. `-pk` breaks ties so pages stay stable.
Constraints: any new default or ordering branch in order_queryset should match an existing index and include a pk tie-breaker. Do not add an index on `order`; that option was rejected because the column is vestigial. The `search` branch still returns the queryset unsorted so relevance ranking applies. The app's own list views send `order=-last_modified_at` explicitly. Changing the default changes the response order for external API clients, so treat it as a customer-visible change.
proposed.applies: Insight list API ordering in InsightViewSet.order_queryset (product_analytics backend)

proposed.title: Changing insight list query ordering requires updating the test_insight.ambr query snapshot
answers: Snapshot test failing after changing insight queryset order
Where are the insight list SQL snapshots stored?
How do I check which ORDER BY the insight list endpoint emits?
proposed.body:
The insight API tests use QueryMatchingTest. The SQL of the list endpoint, including its exact `ORDER BY` and `LIMIT 100`, is captured in products/product_analytics/backend/tests/api/__snapshots__/test_insight.ambr.
Any change to InsightViewSet.order_queryset (or to the annotations and joins on the list queryset) changes that SQL, so the .ambr snapshot must be regenerated in the same change. The current default renders as `ORDER BY "posthog_dashboarditem"."last_modified_at" DESC, "posthog_dashboarditem"."id" DESC`.
The snapshot does not check ordering behaviour. Also add an API-level test in products/product_analytics/backend/tests/api/test_insight.py that asserts the result id order. The existing default-order test sets the vestigial `order` field against the timestamp ordering so that it fails under the old behaviour.
proposed.applies: Tests for products/product_analytics insight API querysets

proposed.title: Insight editor auto-saves (PATCH) on chart-type change: scene-instance guard must use insightId/dashboardId, not insightLogicRef
answers: why does the insight save itself when I change chart type
insight editor exits edit mode and shows 'Insight updated' without clicking Save
how does persistDisplayOptions decide whether to PATCH the insight
isInsightSceneInstance returns wrong value right after opening editor
proposed.body:
Symptom: In the insight editor, picking a new chart type saves the insight without the user clicking Save. The editor leaves edit mode and shows "Insight updated" within about a second. It is an intermittent race that is hard to reproduce.
Root cause: frontend/src/scenes/insights/insightDataLogic.tsx:isInsightSceneInstance compared the props key against insightSceneLogic's `insightLogicRef`. A separate listener sets that ref by rebuilding and mounting a new logic, so it can still be stale right after the scene mounts. persistDisplayOptions then treated the editor's instance as a non-scene instance and sent a PATCH.
Fix pattern: Compare against the reducers `insightSceneLogic.values.insightId` and `dashboardId`, which the URL-matching action sets synchronously. Match `insightId === props.dashboardItemId`, and match `dashboardId` with null and undefined treated as equal (`?? null`). Keep the check that `sceneLogic.values.activeSceneId === Scene.Insight`.
Constraints: In kea scene logics, a `*LogicRef` that a listener builds is not a reliable source for synchronous guards. Use the reducer values that drive it. To regression-test, mock `insightSceneLogic.findMounted` so it returns `{ values: { insightId, dashboardId, insightLogicRef: null } }`. Then assert that the PATCH spy is not called after `persistDisplayOptions` (see the `persistDisplayOptions` describe block in insightDataLogic.test.ts).

proposed.title: Count AI detector 'unavailable' outcomes on the retry-exhausted path, not in the retried activity
answers: why does the ai detector unavailable metric show several failures for one alert check
where is posthog_insight_alerts_ai_detector_checks_total incremented
retried check counted as both failure and success
how to count failed alert checks with Temporal retries
proposed.body:
Symptom: `posthog_insight_alerts_ai_detector_checks_total{outcome="unavailable"}` grows several times per scheduled check, and a check that failed once then succeeded on retry shows up as both a failure and a success.
Root cause: posthog/temporal/alerts/activities.py:evaluate_alert called `record_ai_detector_check_outcome("unavailable")` before re-raising `LLMDetectorUnavailableError`. Temporal retries that activity, so the counter went up once per attempt.
Fix pattern: evaluate_alert just re-raises. posthog/temporal/alerts/activities.py:record_failed_evaluation increments `unavailable` only after `_write_errored_alert_check` has actually written a check and `error.get("code") == LLM_DETECTOR_UNAVAILABLE_ERROR_CODE`.
Constraints: any per-check health metric for a Temporal activity with a retry policy belongs on the terminal path (retry-exhausted, or the final success), never on a failing attempt. Early returns in record_failed_evaluation (disabled alert, next_check_at already in the future, alert deleted) write no check, so they must not count either. Tests in posthog/temporal/tests/test_alerts_activities.py (TestRecordFailedEvaluation, TestEvaluateAlert) pin this behaviour.
proposed.applies: Alert check metrics and outcome counters emitted from Temporal alert activities

proposed.title: evaluate_alert must skip when the reloaded detector type no longer matches the queue prepare picked
answers: AI detector alert ran on a worker without model credentials
what happens if alert detector type changes between prepare and evaluate
uses_llm_detector routing mismatch in CheckAlertWorkflow
why did my alert check get skipped after editing the detector
proposed.body:
Invariant: CheckAlertWorkflow picks the evaluate task queue during prepare, based on the detector type it read (`EvaluateAlertActivityInputs.uses_llm_detector`). Only the AI worker holds the model credentials. posthog/temporal/alerts/activities.py:evaluate_alert reloads the alert with `_load_alert_for_evaluation`, so a detector-type edit made in between could send the check to a worker that cannot run it.
Enforced in evaluate_alert: if `is_llm_detector_config(alert.detector_config) != inputs.uses_llm_detector`, it logs `alerts.skip_detector_type_changed` and returns `EvaluateAlertResult(alert_check_id=None, should_notify=False, ...)` without writing a check or moving `next_check_at`. The next scheduler tick then prepares and routes the alert again, the same way the fingerprint guard skips.
Also: choose the executor (`_LLM_EVALUATE_EXECUTOR`) from the same snapshot you evaluate. Never re-read the alert after routing.
If you add new routing inputs computed in prepare, re-validate them against the reloaded snapshot the same way. Tests that run evaluate_alert must pass a `uses_llm_detector` that matches the alert's detector_config, or the activity skips.
proposed.applies: posthog/temporal/alerts activities that route alert evaluation by detector type

proposed.title: LLMDetectorUnavailableError copy must name the outcome, not a cause; keep the email, in-app and constant in sync
answers: AI detector alert email says could not reach model provider but provider was fine
where is the llm_detector_unavailable message and email wording defined
alert failed email says settings are correct
rename detector_unavailable template context key
proposed.body:
Invariant: `LLMDetectorUnavailableError` covers four outcomes: the rollout flag lookup returned nothing (llm_detector_limits.py), no free model-call slot on the worker, a provider transport failure, and a model reply the judge could not read (all three in judge/llm.py). Owner-facing text must therefore say the detector could not complete the check. It must not name a provider failure, and it must not claim the alert or insight settings are correct, because that path never reads them.

proposed.title: Decimal places 0 is a real value: compare formatting.decimalPlaces against null, never by truthiness
answers: Decimal places set to 0 does nothing on a SQL insight
Big number shows 42.195 instead of 42
table cell ignores zero decimal places under style None
why does decimalPlaces 0 not round
proposed.body:
Symptom: setting Decimal places to 0 on a SQL insight (style None) has no effect; Big number and table cells show 42.195 instead of 42. The Number style rounded correctly because toLocaleString accepts maximumFractionDigits 0.

proposed.title: Chart series data must stay unrounded; decimal places are applied only at display time
answers: metric card total or average is wrong with decimal places set
pie chart total sums rounded values
breakdown bucket sums 0.49+0.49 to 0 or 1
where should decimal places rounding happen for charts

proposed.title: Validate PostHog UUIDT ids by shape only; zod .uuid() rejects them
answers: workflow run cancel button fails with a validation error
cancel invocations API returns 400 for invocation_ids from the runs list
why does z.string().uuid() reject our invocation ids
how to validate a UUIDT in zod
proposed.body:
Symptom: An operator clicks Cancel on a running workflow, or calls the cancel API with `invocation_ids`. The request fails with a validation error and the run keeps going.
Root cause: nodejs/src/cdp/cdp-api.ts:CdpApi checked each id with zod's `z.string().uuid()`, which also checks the RFC version and variant. The invocation store issues UUIDTs. In a UUIDT those nibbles hold a series counter and random bytes, so the check rejected every real id.
Fix pattern: check the shape only with `z.string().refine((id) => UUID.validateString(id, false), msg)`. Keep the shape check: `cancelJobs` binds the ids as `::uuid[]`, so a malformed id must get a 400 at the route and never reach Postgres, where it would cause a 500. On the Python side Django's `UUIDField` already accepts UUIDTs. Do not add a version-aware check to the Django cancel serializer.
Constraints: this applies to any id generated as a UUIDT (posthog.uuidt.UUIDT / nodejs UUIDT). Per the PR, nodejs/src/cdp/schema/hogflow.ts still uses the version-aware rule for `message_category_id` and `template_uuid`, which are also UUIDT-backed. That is a known latent bug of the same kind and was not fixed here. Tests should use real `new UUIDT()` / `str(UUIDT())` ids. A `uuid4` passes either rule and hides this bug.
proposed.applies: Any zod/serializer validation of ids generated as PostHog UUIDTs, especially the CDP hog_flow invocations cancel route

proposed.title: Workflow invocation cancel: Django proxy and CDP route must agree on the id format and the cap
answers: where is workflow run cancellation handled
cancel invocations returns 500 from Django
raising the max invocation ids for cancel
invocation_ids vs all selector in hog flow cancel
proposed.body:
Cancel flows through the Django workflows API, which proxies to the CDP route `POST /api/projects/:team/hog_flows/:flow/invocations/cancel` in nodejs/src/cdp/cdp-api.ts:CdpApi. That route calls `cancelJobs` filtered on (team_id, function_id).
Invariant: the Django cancel serializer and the CDP zod schema must accept the same id set. Both read the same env-driven max-ids cap, so raising the env var lifts both limits together. If the CDP route rejects an id that Django accepted, the route returns a 400 and Django surfaces it to the user as a 500.
The accepted id format must match too. Both sides must accept UUIDTs: Django's UUIDField already does, and CDP uses `UUID.validateString(id, false)`.
Testing: the cancel tests in nodejs/src/cdp/cdp-api.serial.test.ts mostly use `all: true`. The `invocation_ids` path needs its own cases. Run them with `jest --config jest.serial.config.js --testPathPatterns=cdp-api.serial -t cancel`. The Django side is products/workflows/backend/api/test/test_hog_flow_cancel.py, which patches the CDP proxy.

proposed.title: Support draft activity must return a blocked draft on its last attempt, never raise
answers: support ticket stuck on Processing forever
ticket stays in_progress after AI draft fails
what happens when the draft agent returns no JSON
how many retries does the support draft activity get
proposed.body:
Symptom: a support ticket stays on "Processing" (status in_progress) forever when the AI draft agent ends with no message, a prose status sentence instead of JSON, or the agent server crashes.
Root cause: products/conversations/backend/temporal/ai_reply/activities/draft.py:_draft_async raised on every attempt; after the last retry the SupportReplyWorkflow failed before it recorded a result, so the ticket never left in_progress.
Fix pattern: route every failure through draft.py:_give_up. While llm_attempts() < DRAFT_ACTIVITY_MAX_ATTEMPTS it raises DraftNotProducedError so Temporal retries. On the last attempt it returns SupportReplyDraft(reply="", confidence=0.0, verdict="blocked_on_knowledge"). That draft never auto-sends, so a person picks the ticket up. task_run_id is "" when no session was started.
Constraints: products/conversations/backend/temporal/pipeline.py:SupportReplyWorkflow must use RetryPolicy(maximum_attempts=DRAFT_ACTIVITY_MAX_ATTEMPTS) from constants.py, so the activity and the policy agree on which attempt is last. The value stays 2 because changing it affects workflow replay. Any new failure path in the draft activity should call _give_up instead of raising.
proposed.applies: products/conversations AI reply draft activity and its Temporal retry policy

proposed.title: Support draft uses start_raw without output_schema and parses the last valid JSON object
answers: why does the support draft not use output_schema
draft poll fails with no agent message
AI reply used example JSON instead of the real answer
where is the support draft JSON parsed
proposed.body:
The draft call in draft.py:_draft_async uses MultiTurnSession.start_raw and does not pass output_schema. With a schema set, storing the output completes the task run before an agent message reaches the log, so the poll fails with "no agent message". Do not restore output_schema on this call. A Greptile request to restore it was declined for this reason. The five one-shot model calls still keep their JSON schemas.
Parsing happens in draft.py:_parse_draft. It scans every '{' with json.JSONDecoder.raw_decode and returns the LAST dict that validates as SupportReplyDraft, so example or ticket JSON earlier in the text is skipped. The 0–1 confidence coercion (from #105049) still guards bad scores.
If the first turn has no draft, draft.py:_draft_from_session sends one follow-up (_DRAFT_JSON_NUDGE) through send_followup_raw with max_poll_seconds=_DRAFT_NUDGE_POLL_SECONDS (90). The first poll plus the nudge polls must fit inside the activity's 20-minute start_to_close_timeout. EmptyAgentTurnError from start_raw means the run is already ended, so there is nothing to nudge.
Convention: keep nudge and salvage logic in products/conversations. Do not change the shared products/tasks runner, because that would change runner behavior for other callers.
proposed.applies: Support reply draft agent call and its output parsing in products/conversations

proposed.title: Testing the support draft activity: mock start_raw and llm_attempts
answers: how to unit test _draft_async
how to simulate a retry attempt in the draft activity tests
mock MultiTurnSession in conversations tests
proposed.body:
Tests are in products/conversations/backend/temporal/tests/test_pipeline.py (TestDraftWithoutJson, TestUntrustedTicketGuard, TestDiagnosticScopes).
Patch these under DRAFT_MODULE: _hydrate_chunks, resolve_user_id_for_support, get_or_create_support_sandbox_env, and MultiTurnSession.start_raw. Patch start_raw, not start. It returns (session, text) or raises.
To choose the attempt number, patch f"{DRAFT_MODULE}.llm_attempts" to return 1 or 2. Attempt 1 should raise DraftNotProducedError. Attempt 2 should return a blocked draft.

proposed.title: MCP gateway tool discovery after connect/register must warn on failure, with a fixed message
answers: MCP server says Connected but has no tools and no error
desktop add server shows Added but tool list is empty
where is the toast for failed MCP tool listing
should I show the upstream error in the MCP discovery toast
proposed.body:
Symptom: in Desktop, a member connects or adds an MCP server, gets the "Connected"/"Added" message, and the server lists no tools. Nothing says why.
Root cause: both callers of discoverGatewayTools threw its outcome away. In useGatewayServers.ts:useGatewayServers the discover mutation had `onError: () => {}`, and in useRegisterGatewayServer.ts:useRegisterGatewayServer the call ended in `.catch(() => null)`. A `skipped: "no-server"` result (the registry row is gone) resolves successfully, so it never reached any error handler.
Fix pattern: show `toast.warning(DISCOVERY_FAILED)` on a rejected listing and also on `result.skipped === "no-server"`. Do not let it count as a failed connect: registration still returns `created` and `discoveredTools: false`. Leave `skipped === "no-connection"` silent, because the credential is mid-OAuth or needs reauth and the server tag already says "Finishing setup".
Constraints: the toast is a fixed recovery string (DISCOVERY_FAILED, a separate constant in each hook: "Connected, but…" vs "Added, but…"). Never put Error.message or the refresh endpoint's `detail` in it, because that can carry a fragment of the upstream server's response body (CWE-209). Tests in useRegisterGatewayServer.test.tsx check the exact string through a mocked `toast.warning`.
proposed.applies: Desktop MCP gateway hooks that call discoverGatewayTools (products/desktop/packages/ui/src/features/mcp-gateway/hooks)

proposed.title: MCP store proxy returns 502 behind an HTTP(S)_PROXY unless SSRF_TRUSTED_PROXY_URLS names it; do not add an env-proxy fallback
answers: MCP server authenticates but every tool call or sync returns 502
mcp.stripe.com tools 502 through egress proxy
why does pinned_client fail when HTTPS_PROXY is set
SSRF_TRUSTED_PROXY_URLS empty
proposed.body:
Symptom: an MCP connection completes OAuth/DCR but the MCP proxy, tool sync and tool calls all return 502. This happens in deployments that route egress through HTTP(S)_PROXY.
Root cause: the MCP store is the only caller of `pinned_client` (httpx). Its `PinnedTransport` fails closed on a proxied request unless `SSRF_TRUSTED_PROXY_URLS` lists that proxy, and the setting (added in #102376) defaults to empty. OAuth, DCR, discovery and the catalog probe use `requests`, which has no such gate, so they keep working.
Fix pattern: add the egress proxy to `SSRF_TRUSTED_PROXY_URLS` in deployment config, not in code.
Constraints: do not make an empty allowlist fall back to the environment proxy. This was tried and reverted: the proxy branch in `PinnedTransport.handle_request` never rewrites the request to the validated IP, so the fallback silently turns off DNS-rebinding/SSRF protection for URLs users supply.
proposed.applies: Backend MCP store egress through pinned_client / PinnedTransport and SSRF proxy settings
